entities.name: PMID:25441702
observations: Systematic review of 76 articles found multiple valid administrative-data comorbidity indices; performance varied by population and outcome, with c-statistics from ≤0.69 to >0.80.
Elixhauser and Romano-adapted Charlson generally performed better for mortality, while medication-based indices such as Chronic Disease Score performed better for utilization.

entities.name: PMID:34407872
observations: Systematic review in orthopedic populations found Elixhauser and Charlson AUC ranges of 0.70–0.92 and 0.68–0.89, respectively, for in-hospital mortality; it concluded both could be used for mortality adjustment in this setting.
Performance was lower or more variable for longer follow-up outcomes.

entities.name: PMID:29132349
observations: Systematic review of maternal administrative-data indices found only the Maternal Comorbidity Index had been derived and validated specifically in pregnancy/postpartum populations; mortality c-statistic was 0.675.
The review found insufficient evidence to assume general-population Charlson or Elixhauser validity in pregnancy.

entities.name: Administrative indices context-valid
observations: Systematic reviews identify valid administrative-data-derived indices, especially Charlson/Quan/Romano and Elixhauser/van Walraven, but no single index is universally optimal.
Index selection should match data availability, population, and outcome.
